summary: Jeffrey Samuels specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2002) under Karen Christina Lang and studied under W. S. Karunatillake, later serving as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University.

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Brown University (~1968–1972) and Princeton University (PhD ~1972–1976), he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass works in Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of North Carolina Wilmington and University of Tennessee, he earned his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen, subsequently teaching at UCLA and UC San Diego as a lecturer.

Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, having previously studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Her academic career includes posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she served as assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

Jens Braarvig specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He served as a professor at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (~2001) and at the University of Oslo (2003).

Jens Peter Laut works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He served on the Leitungskommission of the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008) and held a post at the University of Göttingen (~2008–2020).

Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After earning his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1994–1999) under Josef Simon, he became Professor and Institute Managing Director at the University of Bern (~2009).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After studies and a habilitation at Munich and Göttingen, he held professorships at Humboldt University (1995–2001), Free University of Berlin (~1995–1999), and University of Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London in 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld is a sinologist and art historian who completed his BA and PhD at Stanford University. He served as Chair of Art History at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Professor of Chinese Art History at Princeton (~2001–2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a scholar of linguistics and Central Asian studies. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961), where he served as professor from 1969 and director from 1977 to 1991.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1926) and under Antoine Meillet (~1921–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1927–1945) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).

Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011 and served as Junior Professor in South Asian History of Religion at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).
Ji Hao is a sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Minnesota under the supervision of Paul Rouzer. He held an academic post at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Wenhui Yang (~1904–1911). He founded and served as head of the China Institute of Inner Learning from around 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. After completing his doctoral dissertation at Harvard University (attested 2002) under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello, he became a professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and held a researcher position at Komazawa University (both attested 2015).
Jianteng is a Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi, whom he succeeded in 2005.
Jiaqi Wang was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He was a disciple of Gangkar Rinpoche and was also recorded as a PhD student at Columbia University (attested 2026).
